newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IBM wants Hungary to sign WTO deals.
newsitem.headline: IBM wants Hungary to sign WTO deals.

text.p: Hungary's failure to sign two World Trade Organisation (WTO) agreements hinders IBM Hungary's exports to the United States, International Business Machine Corp. officials said Tuesday.

"For contracts with the U.S. government, those treaties are required," Walter Meizer, general manager of Germany's IBM Speichersysteme GmbH, a unit of IBM Storage Systems Division, told a news conference.

Dieter Munk, general manager of IBM's Hungarian hard drive plant in Szekesfehervar in western Hungary, said the United States gives preferential treatment to those importers who have signed the WTO agreements on general purchases and information technology.
Munk said IBM had invested $100 million in Hungary since early 1995 and by the end of 1997 will have created over 3,500 jobs directly or through IBM projects.
The Hungarian plant assembles and tests 3.5-inch disk drives for desktop computers and 2.5-inch drives for mobile appliances.

The parts come from Southeast Asia, Germany and Italy, and the final product is exported. Forty percent goes to IBM's own PC companies and 60 percent to other manufacturers. Munk said that in 1996 some 60 percent of the plant's exports went to the United States.
Last year, the plant produced 1 million disk drives, and IBM plans to triple output this year.
